defect_list.description: The note said every use case needs delegated and managed access to multiple data sources. The text (p.8 ll.157-163) says this only of use case 1. Use case 2 is 'as with use case #1' with elevated risk, and use case 3 concerns entitlements and authorization in deployment pipelines.

gateway_control_ko stated flatly that MINT verifies OAuth responses and tokens and requires encrypted transport. That reads as current behavior, which the guide does not establish. It is now framed as a mapping item, with current support not confirmed by the note.
The abstract does not say the paper sets no controls or requirements. That was the author's inference, attributed to the abstract. It now reads as an observation about the body text.
'native delegation' was rendered '기본 위임' (default delegation). It is now '내장 위임' (built-in delegation).

Two checked facts were missing. The CSRC record gives published 2026-02-05, comments due 2026-04-02 and 'CLOSED'. The 2026-09-29 NIST news says feedback is now taken on a rolling basis with no fixed comment period. Both were added. The other date and status claims were confirmed (NIST initiative page: created 2026-02-17, updated 2026-08-14, deadline April 2; news and hub: 600+ commenters, DevSecOps first use case, draft project description planned; PDF metadata creation date 2026-02-04).

defect_list.description: The paraphrase follows the 2024 OJ wording, which lists 'AI system, tools, services, components, processes' as what the third party supplies. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art. 1 point 12(b), added 'AI model' to that list. The note's own pitfalls say Art. 25(4) was amended, but the provision text did not reflect it. I read the amending text on the Publications Office XHTML to confirm.

gateway_control_ko said the product 'warns when the ledger retention is set under 6 months' and implied the ledger covers the provider log duty. That feature is not an established product capability, and Art. 19 concerns the provider's own logs. Reworded as a requirement candidate with an explicit limit.

gateway_control_ko said the ledger is supplied as evidence of the deployer's retained logs and that retention is set by policy. The duty covers logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system, which the gateway ledger does not replace. Reworded as a possible supporting record and a requirement candidate.

The obligation text also covers 73(1) (report to the market surveillance authority of the Member State where the incident occurred) and 73(5) (initial incomplete report), so the ref range was too narrow. The anchor sits in 73(2) and the 15-day, 2-day and 10-day periods are correct. The ref now reads Art. 73(1)-(5).
POL-07 concerns an external provider's handling of documents (storage, reuse, third-party sharing). It is unrelated to obtaining the provider's instructions for use. Removed it and kept POL-02.
POL-07 concerns an external provider's document handling, not downstream-provider documentation on model capabilities and limits. Removed it and kept POL-03.

The summary said the regulation is enforced separately by Member States. Under Art. 88(1) the Commission has exclusive powers to supervise and enforce the general-purpose AI model obligations in Chapter V. Corrected the sentence.
The title left out the OJ title clause 'and amending Regulations (EC) No 300/2008, ... and Directives ...', which appears on the first page of the extract. Restored the full official title.
The note gave 'Chapter III Sections 1-3' as Arts 9-27. Section 1 starts at Art. 6 (Arts 6-7), Section 2 is Arts 8-15 and Section 3 is Arts 16-27. Changed to Arts 6-27.

The note said the Publications Office copyright page tells readers to see EUR-Lex's own notice for EU legal documents and OJ content. The page I fetched says only that reusing content from EUR-Lex, European Data, EU Tenders and CORDIS is governed by each site's own notice, and that Cellar re-use terms are obtained by contacting the Publications Office. Reworded. The distribution decision is unchanged.
actor is 'operator', which the Act defines as including importers, distributors and others. Art. 4 addresses only providers and deployers. The schema has no combined value, so I left it.

Gateway-control wording in several rows is a design intent or requirement candidate rather than a confirmed product capability (for example, the Art. 6 'high-risk candidate' labels and the Art. 14 approve/deny/revoke flows). defect_list.description: 요약이 문서의 권고를 '건별 사람 승인'이라고 적었다. 원문(p.15, p.22)은 의사결정 단계의 필수 사람 승인과 오류 비용이 큰 행동의 사람 검토·승인 체크포인트를 권고할 뿐 호출 건별 승인을 요구하지 않는다.
함정 항목이 22쪽의 권고를 '건별 승인 요구'라고 표기했다. 원문은 고비용 행동에 사람 승인 체크포인트를 두라는 취지다.

gateway_control_ko가 '권한 축소' 자동화를 제품 기능처럼 적었다. 제품이 갖춘 것은 연결 자동 중지다. 권한 자동 축소는 요구사항 후보로 표기했다.

defect_list.description: Art. 45(1) is permissive ("may take place ... shall not require any specific authorisation"), but the provision was tagged strength=mandatory. The guide reserves mandatory for must/shall duties.

obligation_ko listed "제3국 이전과 보호조치 문서" as if safeguards documentation were required for every third-country transfer. Art. 30(1)(e) requires safeguards documentation only for transfers under the second subparagraph of Art. 49(1).

gateway_control_ko said the alert timestamp in the ledger "proves" the 72-hour start. The legal trigger is the controller "becoming aware", which is not the same as the alert time. The control also implied a legal conclusion.

The anchor began in the tail of Art. 13(2)(e) ("possible consequences of failure to provide such data") and only then reached (f). The same words also appear in Art. 14(2)(g) and Art. 15(1)(h). Replaced with a (f)-specific verbatim phrase.
POL-08 (connection approval and user consent) does not match a notice duty about automated decisions or the gateway_control text. POL-38 kept.
gateway_control_ko stated retention expiry, deletion and deletion evidence as existing capabilities. Reworded as a requirement to build.

The note has 30 provisions, above the guide's 8-25 range. All 30 are text-supported, so none were removed, as the instructions say not to delete supported provisions. check_notes.py does not flag the count.
The title omits the OJ heading suffix "(Text with EEA relevance)". This is cosmetic; the rest of the official title matches the PDF.

doc_level_changes: No document-level fields were changed.

Verified against the CELLAR SPARQL endpoint (publications.europa.eu): signature 2016-04-27, entry into force 2016-05-24, application 2018-05-25, in-force=1, end of validity 9999-12-31. Three corrigenda R(01), R(02) and R(03) are linked and no amending act is linked.

Verified against the European Parliament Legislative Observatory page for 2025/0360(COD): COM(2025)0837 published 19/11/2025, status 'Awaiting committee decision', no adoption. The page lists the procedure as amending Regulation 2016/679.
Verified Art. 99(1) and 99(2) against the extract. Publication 4.5.2016 plus 20 days gives 24.5.2016, and the Regulation applies from 25.5.2018.

remaining_concerns: EUR-Lex returns HTTP 202 with an empty body to curl and WebFetch (both the ELI page and the legal notice). I could not re-fetch the legal notice live. The licence text was checked only against the author's staged copy (web/eurlex_legal_notice.html). Status and dates were checked through CELLAR and the Legislative Observatory.

The Art. 22(1) gateway_control_ko proposes human approval for high-risk tools. The note's pitfalls already warn that this may not remove the 'solely automated' character, and that is left to the organisation to judge.

Art. 25(1) is tagged theme=security_risk_management. Data protection by design could equally fit data_minimisation_retention_deletion or secure_development_supply_chain. This is a judgement call and was not changed.
The PDF is the original OJ text without the three corrigenda. The note says so, but any citation should be checked against the corrected consolidated text.

defect_list.description: obligation_ko said organizations 'must document' risk management with AI RMF. The text says only that once tolerance is defined, the AI RMF 'can be used to manage risks and to document' them. The 'should' applies to following existing regulations and to defining reasonable risk tolerance.

The text says higher initial prioritization 'may be called for' (permissive), not a 'should'. Strength was 'recommended'. gateway_control_ko also stated flatly that personal-data calls are designated high-risk. Changed to 'informative' and reworded the control as something policy can be configured to do.
The source says transparency is 'often necessary' for actionable redress. The note dropped 'often'.
gateway_control_ko stated a role-separation and self-approval-ban permission model as an existing feature. That is not in the MINT capability vocabulary. Reworded to say it can be configured.
gateway_control_ko stated the tool catalog with intended-use, risk-grade and approval-type fields as an existing feature. Hedged to 'can'.
gateway_control_ko said evidence of description/behaviour tests is kept, as if already done. Hedged to 'can keep'.
obligation_ko said 'human override' (사람의 번복). The source says only 'appeal and override' and does not say the override is by a human. Removed the added actor.

Theme was agentic_ai, but the passage covers human roles and oversight across human-AI configurations. The document never mentions agents (grep confirmed). agentic_ai could imply NIST addresses agentic AI. Changed to human_oversight. The MINT-interpretation caveat in gateway_control_ko is kept.

POL-02 is only loosely related to the AI system definition, and the claim that read/write/execute logs let autonomy level be told apart afterwards is a stretch. This is not clearly wrong, so it was left and flagged.
The note has 29 provisions, above the guide's 8-25 range. The checker passes. All provisions are supported by the text, so none were removed.

doc_level_changes: None needed. Re-checked against the NIST official page fetched 2026-10-17. Released January 26, 2023. The page says 'The AI RMF 1.0 is being revised as part of the White House AI Action Plan', and no draft or successor ID exists on the AI RMF page or the AI RMF Development page. The generative AI profile NIST-AI-600-1 was released 2024-07-26. The Critical Infrastructure Profile concept note was released 2026-04-07. The page links the PDF at nvlpubs and the DOI 10.6028/NIST.AI.100-1, and the local PDF SHA-256 matches provenance.json. The 'review no later than 2028' sentence is on PDF p.3 (Update Schedule and Versions) of the extract. The NIST series page lists NIST AI 100 under the Technical Report Series. The extract has no copyright notice, and Fig. 2 is marked 'Modified from OECD (2022)'. The license_notice paraphrase and the distribution_reason hedge match these sources.
remaining_concerns: NIST says AI RMF 1.0 is being revised, so subcategory numbers and wording may change. The note already says this in key_dates and pitfalls_ko. Re-check before citing in requirements.
The licence grant covers works authored by NIST employees. The document does not state its authorship, and Fig. 2 is OECD-derived. The note leaves figure inclusion to central review.
gateway_control_ko entries are MINT proposals. Even after hedging, some read as declarative statements, as in the exemplar. They are not claims of legal compliance.
Page refs use printed page numbers (PDF page minus 5). All 29 refs were checked against the extract page markers and are consistent.

defect_list.description: gateway_control_ko가 '게이트웨이를 거치지 않는 직접 연결을 차단·탐지한다'고 현재형으로 적었으나 이는 제품 기본 기능 목록에 없는 후보 기능(POL-12)이다.
'SIEM으로 내보내는 연동을 제공한다'는 제품이 이미 제공한다는 뜻이라 근거가 없다. 요구사항으로 낮췄다.

defect_list.description: The pitfall said the 24h, 72h and 1-month deadlines all run from when the entity becomes aware. Art. 23(4)(d) runs the one-month final report from submission of the incident notification (the provision entry itself was correct). Rewritten.

The second sentence said minimal processing is required for incident reports and logs. Art. 2(14) does not say that. Also omitted single points of contact from the list of processors. Sentence removed and the actor list completed.
'감사 방해' dropped the qualifier in (a)(iv): the obstructed audits or monitoring must be ones the authority ordered after finding an infringement. Qualifier restored.

Said the product provides a 24-hour deadline timer and owner notification, which are not part of the stated MINT capabilities. Reworded: the alert time is recorded in the ledger as evidence, and the timer and notification are only feature candidates.
Asserted that the export feature already generates results directly from the ledger and records a hash. Reworded as a requirement candidate.

Said the equivalent duty is under 'Arts. 21 and 23'. Art. 4(1) says 'obligations laid down in this Directive'; the Art. 21(1)-(2) and 23(1)-(6) equivalence tests are in Art. 4(2). Also omitted the rule that the Directive still applies to entities the sector act does not cover. Fixed both.
'제21조 요건 준수' should be 'particular requirements of Article 21'. Fixed.

The sentence about stating the purpose of a request comes from Art. 32(3), not 32(2). Ref changed to Art. 32(2)-(3). Also corrected 'regular and ad hoc audits' to regular and targeted audits plus ad hoc audits.
The turnover base is the total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year of the undertaking the entity belongs to. Added.
Described Art. 32 as 'ex ante and ex post'. Art. 32 does not use those words and the recitals were not read. Art. 33(1) does say 'ex post'. Reworded to what the articles say.
The statement that NIS2 does not replace the GDPR rests on Art. 2(12) (without prejudice), not only 2(14) and 35. Cite added.
POL-07 covers checking an external provider's document handling. The provision is about whether MINT itself is an in-scope service type. Link removed.
POL-44 (revocation and disconnection) does not relate to telling service recipients about a cyber threat. Link removed, POL-43 kept.
The text lists criteria (a) and (b) with no 'or'. The note's '또는' follows the usual alternative reading. Left unchanged.
Trust service providers have a 24h (not 72h) deadline under the derogation in 23(4). Not mentioned in the note. Left unchanged since it affects few MINT customers.
The note has 30 provisions; NOTE_GUIDE suggests 8-25. check_notes.py does not flag this. No provision was removed because all 30 anchors and refs are supported.

defect_list.description: The note said the CRA acts as an indirect requirement (supplier due diligence, SBOM, support period) on customers who adopt external MCP servers. The regulation puts no direct duty on such customers. Annex II item 9 makes SBOM access a manufacturer's choice, and item 7 only requires the support-period end date.

The note said the definitions of 'actively exploited vulnerability' and 'severe incident' sit in lower-level documents and were not read. They are in the Regulation itself (Art. 3(42) and Art. 14(5)). Only the Art. 16 platform design, the delegated and implementing acts under Art. 14(9) and 14(10), and the rest of Art. 3 are unread.
The summary listed 'products placed on the market without vulnerabilities'. Annex I Part I(2)(a) says 'without known exploitable vulnerabilities'.

The paraphrases dropped the condition from the Annex I Part I(2) lead-in ('on the basis of the cybersecurity risk assessment ... and where applicable'). The (e) confidentiality item was also overstated as 'protect with state-of-the-art encryption'. The text gives encryption as an example ('such as by encrypting ... and by using other technical means').
No pitfall flagged that the Annex I Part I(2) requirements are risk-based and apply 'where applicable' (Art. 13(3)), while Part II has no such qualifier. Added one.

The note said 'the scouting stage deems 2024-12-10 the date of entry into force'. That is an internal-process leak, and the date is not stated in the PDF (Art. 71(1) only says the twentieth day after publication). Rewrote the field with the signing date, the OJ date and Art. 71(1), and cited the Commission CRA summary page for the 2024-12-10 date, which I fetched and which states it.
The text referred to 'the ENISA platform news mentioned by the scouting stage'. Reworded to state plainly that the platform's actual launch was not confirmed.

The title omitted the 'and amending Regulations (EU) No 168/2013 and (EU) No 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2020/1828' part. Restored it as printed on page 1 of the PDF.

The note said MINT 'requests the manufacturer's risk assessment document'. The CRA does not give users that document. It goes into the technical documentation for authorities (Art. 13(4), 13(22)). Users get the Annex II information, which includes the support-period end date. Reworded as a candidate and as a duty with no gateway equivalent.

The text said to 'stop the function until fixed or isolated and notify the supplier'. POL-39 only says to isolate or stop use when remediation is impossible within the deadline, and says nothing about notifying the supplier. Reworded to follow POL-39 and marked as a candidate.
The text said the ledger 'supports the manufacturer's notification schedule'. Reworded as a candidate evidence source that does not replace the manufacturer's notification or deadline management.

The text implied the ledger provides 'calls suspected of malicious code execution'. Detecting malicious code execution is not an established MINT capability. Reworded as a candidate: call history and anomaly alerts, with no 'severe incident' determination.
The text said 'admin routes are restricted to administrator authentication'. That is a product claim with no basis in the guide's capability vocabulary or in the CRA text. Removed that clause.

gateway_control이 원장 보존을 1년으로 '설정'하고 계약 보안 조항을 '요구'한다고 단정함. 규칙은 개인정보 보존도 말하는데 원장은 개인정보를 최소화·마스킹하므로 충돌 가능성을 가림. 백업(d)과 처리자 계약(f)은 고객 절차임.
POL-15(서버별 인증정보 분리)는 규칙 6(1)과 무관.
'개인정보 본문은 보존 대상에서 제외하거나 마스킹'으로 규칙의 개인정보·로그 1년 보존 요건을 충족하는 것처럼 읽힘. 개인정보 보존 범위는 고객 판단이라고 명시하도록 수정.
'등록 사용자' 임계값은 인도 내(in India) 등록 사용자이고 다른 법상 보존 필요 시 예외(8(1))인데 누락. pitfalls에서는 임계값을 '넘는'(초과)으로 적었으나 원문은 not less than(이상).

gateway_control이 후보 기능을 현재 동작처럼 현재형('표시한다', '강화한다', '갱신한다', '제공한다', '둔다')으로 서술. 후보·조건 표현으로 수정.

표시 없는 콘텐츠 제공은 '可以'(재량)이고 6개월 로그 보존은 그렇게 제공하는 경우에 걸리는 조건부 의무인데 무조건 의무처럼 읽혔다. timing_ko도 조건을 빠뜨렸다.

'고객이 제공자인 경우에만 관련된다'는 제10조제2항(모든 조직·개인 대상 삭제·위조 금지)과 제10조제1항(이용자 선언 의무)과 모순된다.
GB 45438-2025 번호와 표준 명칭은 추출문에 없는 기억 기반 사실이다. CAC 해설 페이지로 강제성 표준의 존재, 2025년 제3호 공고, 2025-09-01 동시 시행은 확인했다. 번호는 공식 페이지에서 확인하지 못했다.
적용 범위 조항을 mandatory로 표기했다. 의무 조항이 아니므로 informative가 맞다.
gateway_control이 '중국 시장 대상'이라는 본문에 없는 지역 한정을 넣고, 기록 절차를 기존 기능처럼 '표시한다'고 썼다.
gateway_control의 '도입 심사의 동작 시험 범위가 아니다'는 근거 없는 주장이고 제4조제2항의 '도입 시험 항목으로 둘 수 있다'와 모순된다.
POL-07(외부 제공자의 문서 저장·재사용·제3자 제공 확인)은 사용자 협의에 표시 방법을 명시하는 의무와 맞지 않는다.
'부문규장'이라는 분류는 본문으로 뒷받침되지 않는다. 통지(通字)로 인쇄·배포된 문서이므로 행정적 성격의 규범 문서로 고쳤다. 저작권법 제5조 제1호 조문과 2021-06-01 시행은 商务部 DB에서 확인했다(현행 유효). 보존본은 사이트 화면 구성이 포함된 HTML이라 사이트 화면 구성·로고·'© 版权所有'는 근거에서 제외한다고 명시했다.

The text says 明显偏激 (obviously extreme or radical) questions must be refused. The note rendered it as 'biased' (편향), which changes the meaning. The text also says 'should be able to answer all other questions', which the note weakened.

POL-22 (per-request execution authorisation) and POL-38 do not correspond to a model's output pass rate or refusal behaviour. The claim that the gateway records denial reasons as evidence of model refusal conflated gateway policy denials with model refusals.
The text says the gateway 'manages and confirms' dev/test/prod separation. The provision concerns the provider's training vs inference environments, so this does not evidence compliance.

The obligation also covers 6.2 a) (public disclosure of target groups, scenes and uses on the homepage), so the ref is now 6.2 a)-c). The note limited disclosure to the 'service terms'; the text says homepage, service agreement or other easily viewed places.
The obligation also paraphrases 6.4 a), so the ref is now 6.4 a)-b). The list of channels is 'including but not limited to', which the note omitted.
The text says 达到一定次数 ('reaches a certain number'). The note said 'exceeds' (초과).
POL-05 (Tool description vs actual behaviour test) is unrelated to the size of a model-output test question bank, which is informative only.
gateway_control_ko said intake or application forms 'confirm' or 'contain' items, as if this already happened. Reworded as candidate or policy items under POL-07 or the intake review.

The quoted passage is in 引言 (Introduction), not the 서문. The LIB-M09 instrument was called '관리 규정' in scope_ko but '관리 잠정 방법' in pitfalls. The scope_ko sentence about LIB-M09 was garbled; it is now one clear unconfirmed statement.

The technical committee was named with its old Korean name (정보보안). The foreword says 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (SAC/TC260).

The note called the 2025-06-30 date unconfirmed and had not checked status on an official register. I checked openstd.samr.gov.cn: status 现行, published 2025-04-25, effective 2025-11-01, issued by SAMR and SAC. The TC260 page shows 2025-06-30 as the full-text posting date.

defect_list.description: 'microenterprise'를 '소기업'(small enterprise)으로 번역해 면제 범위를 잘못 서술했다. 제3조 제60호는 직원 10명 미만이고 연 매출 또는 연 자산 총액이 200만 유로 이하인 금융기관(거래소, 중앙청산소, 거래정보저장소, 중앙예탁기관 제외)으로 정의한다.
'최소 연 1회' 검토라고만 적었으나 본문(제6조 제5항)은 초소기업에 대해 '정기적으로'로 완화한다. 시행 근거 자료로 쓰는 경우를 위해 예외를 추가했다. 또 이 조항과 맞지 않는 POL-37 연결을 제거했다.
topic_ko가 사이버 공격 시 영향 자산의 자동 격리를 의무처럼 적었다. 본문은 자동 격리 메커니즘을 'may include'(예시)로 두고, 의무는 네트워크 연결 인프라를 즉시 단절·분할할 수 있게 설계하는 것(shall)이다.
중대한 사이버 위협 시 고객에게 보호 조치를 알릴 의무에서 'where applicable'(해당하는 경우) 한정을 빠뜨려 의무를 무조건처럼 적었다.
'등록부를 연 1회 감독 당국에 보고'처럼 읽히게 적었다. 본문은 최소 연 1회 신규 계약 수·제공자 범주·계약 유형·서비스와 기능을 보고하고, 등록부 전체는 요청 시 제출하도록 한다. 또 등록부 수준에 'sub-consolidated'가 빠져 있었고 감독 당국 제출용 내보내기를 이미 있는 기능처럼 적었다.
gateway_control_ko가 게이트웨이가 외부 서버의 처리·저장 위치 변경을 감지하고 데이터 반환·삭제를 확인한다고 주장했다. 근거가 없는 기능 주장이며 연결 주소 변경 재승인(POL-40)과 계약·도입 검토 절차로 한정해 다시 썼다.
'게이트웨이 장애 시 차단(fail-closed) 동작'을 제품 문서에 명시한다고 적어 근거 없는 현재 동작을 전제했다. 후보 방안으로 낮췄다. 관련성이 낮은 POL-42도 제거했다.
구성·연결·의존성 매핑을 '핵심 자산'에 한정해 적었으나 본문 제4항은 핵심 자산 매핑과 별개로 자산의 구성과 상호 연결·의존성 전반을 매핑하도록 한다.
MINT가 금융기관의 ICT 제3자로서 제29·30·31조의 영향을 받는다고 단정했다. 이는 ICT 서비스 정의(제3조 제21호) 해당 여부와 지정 여부에 달린 법적 판단이며 본문으로 뒷받침되지 않는다. 해당할 수 있다는 조건부 서술로 고쳤다.
'제28조 제9~10항이 재위탁 표준을 위임'했다고 적었다. 제28조 제9항은 등록부 표준 서식, 제10항은 핵심 기능 ICT 서비스 이용 정책의 세부 내용이고, 재위탁 관련 기술표준은 제30조 제5항이다.

중앙 검증 증거에 없는 세부 내용('© European Union, 1998-2026', 국제회계기준 예시, '브라우저로 직접 열람')을 EUR-Lex 법적 고지 인용에 넣었다. 검증 단계에서 해당 페이지는 curl로 열리지 않아(HTTP 202) 직접 재확인하지 못했다. 중앙 검증 문구만 남기고 인용 출처를 명시했으며 배포 판단(public-under-license, 보존 PDF에 별도 조건 없음)은 유지했다.
'사본 열람 권리'로 적었으나 본문은 현장에서 사본을 취할(take copies) 권리다.
원장이 사건을 '심각도와 함께' 기록한다고 적었으나 근거가 없다. 입력 자료로 활용 가능한 수준으로 낮췄다.
보고서 첨부용 내보내기 기능을 이미 있는 것처럼 적었다. 근거 자료 활용과 후보로 낮췄다.
obligation_ko가 패치·업데이트 정책(제4항 (f))까지 다루는데 ref에는 (e)만 있었다.
탐지 메커니즘 조항을 incident_reporting으로 분류했다. 보고가 아닌 탐지·모니터링이므로 security_risk_management로 바꿨다.
의무 주체(금융기관)에 GDPR 용어인 'controller'를 썼다. 규정이 쓰지 않는 용어라 'operator'로 바꿨다.
공식 제목에서 'and amending Regulations ...' 부분이 빠져 있었다. Publications Office 메타데이터의 전체 제목으로 고쳤다.
발효일(2023-01-16)과 서명일이 없었다. Publications Office SPARQL 메타데이터와 제64조(20일째, 관보 2022-12-27)로 확인해 추가했고 유효 상태(in force, 종료일 9999-12-31, 이 규정을 개정하는 법령 기록 없음)를 병기했다.
제2조를 읽지 않았다고 했으나 제2조는 ICT 제3자 서비스 제공자를 포함해 적용 대상을 열거하고 제3항에서 제외 대상을 둔다. 검증 단계에서 제1~4조를 확인해 범위 서술을 보강했다. reading_scope의 '제8~13조(제7조 제외)' 표현은 앞뒤가 맞지 않아 정리했다.
EUR-Lex ELI 페이지는 curl로 HTTP 202(본문 없음)가 와서 직접 확인하지 못했다. Publications Office Cellar 알림과 SPARQL로 ELI reg/2022/2554/oj 매핑, 제목, 서명일, 유효 상태를 확인했다. limitations_ko에 명시했다.

remaining_concerns: EUR-Lex 공식 페이지와 법적 고지 페이지는 이 환경에서 열리지 않았다(HTTP 202). 공식 페이지는 Publications Office 메타데이터로 대신 확인했고, 라이선스 문구는 중앙 검증 증거만 인용했다.
높음 또는 중간 결함이 있던 조항이 약 7~8개(21개 중)로 기준선 부근이었다. 대부분 수식어 누락, 번역 용어, 기능 과장이었고 모두 본문과 대조해 고쳤다. 발명된 의무는 발견하지 못했다.
gateway_control_ko의 일부 문장은 여전히 MINT 기능 어휘 수준의 설명이며 각 기능의 실제 구현 여부는 이 검증에서 확인하지 않았다.
제7조, 제13~16조, 제20~27조(TLPT 포함), 제31조 이후는 읽지 않았고 위임 규정(RTS/ITS)의 구체 기한·서식은 이 노트 범위 밖이다. 'major'와 'significant'를 모두 '중대한'으로 옮긴 점은 독자가 구분해 읽어야 한다.

defect_list.description: Penalty caps were 10x too low. The Schedule says 250 crore (rupees 2.5 billion = 25억), 200 crore (20억), 150 crore (15억) and 50 crore (5억). The note wrote 2.5억, 2억, 1.5억 and 0.5억 in the summary, s.8(5), s.8(6), s.33 and the pitfalls. The Schedule row-to-amount mapping itself (1=250, 2=200, 3=200, 4=150, 5=Rs 10,000, 6=as per the s.28 proceedings, 7=50) matches the extract.

Status was 'in_force'. The note's own key_dates say the text read gives only a commencement power (s.1(2)) and the scout's 2025-11-13 claim was unverified. Secondary sources (a law-firm article and a PIB explainer) describe phased commencement from mid-Nov 2025: Board provisions at once, consent-manager provisions after about 12 months, and the core duties (ss.3-17 etc.) after about 18 months, i.e. around May 2027. If so, the duties the note cites were probably not yet applicable on 2026-10-17. The sources disagree on 13 vs 14 November. The official MeitY page is a JS shell with no text and WebFetch returned 403, so I could not read the Gazette commencement notification.

The old key_dates repeated the scout's unverified 2025-11-13 claim and gave no phased schedule. Rewritten to state the assent and publication date of 2023-08-11 (from the Gazette), then the secondary-source phased schedule explicitly marked unconfirmed.

The actor was 'controller' and the strength 'mandatory', but the text says the Central Government 'may, by notification, restrict' transfers. It is a permissive power of the government, and a restriction binds only once notified.
The note said the Board 'imposes' the penalty and set strength to mandatory. The text says the Board 'may' impose it, after an inquiry finds the breach significant and after a hearing.
Strength was 'mandatory', but s.7 is a permission ('may process ... for any of following uses').
A commencement clause was tagged 'mandatory'. It is not an obligation on any actor.

The paraphrase of s.6(6) left out the exception for processing required or authorised by law without consent. s.6(10) applies only where consent is the basis of processing. The ref also cited sub-s.(5), which the obligation does not paraphrase.

The note said the purpose is deemed no longer served if the Data Principal does not 'contact or exercise rights'. The text requires both: she neither approaches the fiduciary nor exercises any right, for a prescribed period (s.8(8)(a) 'and' (b)).
POL-45 (token and API-key recovery) was linked to erasing personal data on consent withdrawal, and the gateway control mentioned token recovery. That is not what the provision requires.
The topic labelled the Data Processor '수탁자', which clashes with the note's term for Data Fiduciary.

The note said the 2024-10-15 publication date was not checked. It is now confirmed on the official page, which is the only verified date. Whether a later edition exists is still unknown.

It says website Contents are copyright-protected and may not be reproduced, republished, uploaded, transmitted or distributed without CSA's prior written permission, unless otherwise provided. The PDF text carries no licence or copyright notice, and it is served from a separate host (isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg), so the terms do not clearly cover it. No free-use statement was found. The local-only decision stands and matches the central evidence (nothing for CSA). The notice now states exactly this.
'Not mandatory' comes from section 1 (p.3). Only 'no prescriptive controls or requirements' comes from 3.3 (p.10). The note cited 3.3 for both.
The note said a separate agentic addendum covers the scope this document excludes. Nothing in the text or on the official page supports that, and the sentence was garbled.
It stated 'fail-closed when the policy engine is unavailable' as a default. That is not in the guide's capability vocabulary and was not in the source. Reworded as a candidate control.
It claimed 'input validation' as an applied control, which matches none of the linked POLs. Removed and reworded as a candidate.

It claimed the product records a 'residual risk acceptor' and shows a 're-assessment required' flag. Neither feature is in the guide's capability vocabulary. Reworded as a candidate way to produce evidence.
POL-01 (distribution provenance/integrity) does not relate to training or threat modelling. The sentence about checking supplier threat models at intake had no source. Both removed.

Theme access_control_identity did not fit. The text is about tracking, authenticating and version-controlling AI assets, not user identity. Changed to security_risk_management. 'Contract lock' and 'policy bundle' are undefined product terms and were removed.
It said the product provides a flow that exports the ledger per incident. Reworded as using the audit ledger to reconstruct call history (candidate).
The specific detail '300자 초과 인자는 앞부분과 해시' (arguments over 300 characters kept as a prefix plus hash) is not supported by the source or the capability vocabulary. Removed.

Anchors, refs, modality (all 'should' or 'good practice', so recommended), actors, timing and pol_ids match the text and are plausible. The wording of gateway_control_ko still reads as a present-tense capability in places, which is the exemplar's style, so I left it.

defect_list.description: The note called the Art. 7 business duty a 'duty to endeavor to cooperate'. The English text and the Japanese original (協力しなければならない) say utilization business operators 'must cooperate' with national and local government measures. Only the efficiency and new-industry part is an endeavor duty. Also a wrong claim that business obligations are limited to endeavor-to-cooperate.

obligation_ko said the guidelines are the legal basis of business soft-law guidelines. Art. 13 only says the national government is to establish guidelines in line with international norms and take other measures. gateway_control_ko also asserted a link to LIB-M42 as a basis for Japanese customer requirements, and pitfalls repeated the soft-law-basis claim. The text does not support the link.

'규제 강화 여부는 이 검토에서 달라질 수 있다' appears nowhere in the text. The article only requires a review of how the Act is in effect and, if the government finds it necessary, measures based on the result. Removed it. Also removed gateway_control_ko wording that described a customer-requirements check as an existing practice.

The note contained the leaked process wording '스카우트 단계 ... 보고했으며 이 노트에서 확인하지 않았다' and an unverified 2025-09-01 date. The Cabinet Office page I fetched says the Act was promulgated and partly in force on 2025-06-04 (令和7年6月4日) and fully in force on 9月1日, including the Strategic Headquarters provisions. The page prints no year, so 2025 is inferred from context. Rewrote key_dates with the source and the caveat. The Cabinet Order itself was not read.

The note said the terms page was unreadable (HTTP 401) and set local-only. The scout had probed /en/index/logo-use, the wrong page. https://www.japaneselawtranslation.go.jp/en/index/terms returned HTTP 200 and says content on the site is under the Public Data License v1.0 (PDL1.0) unless stated otherwise, with copyright held by the Ministry of Justice. PDL1.0, read on digital.go.jp, permits free commercial use, copying, public transmission, translation and modification. Conditions: source citation, an edited-statement and no misrepresentation as an unaltered original, and third-party rights. The logo is excluded. The staged PDF has no contrary notice. Rewrote license_notice and distribution_reason and set distribution to public-under-license with attribution conditions.

The English text is passive ('measures must be implemented') with no stated addressee. The Japanese uses 施策が講じられなければならない, policy measures, and Art. 4(1) puts the duty to implement measures under the basic principles on the national government. Kept actor=authority but added to obligation_ko that it is an addressee-less basic principle with no direct business duty. defect_list.description: The note gave only the PIB home page. I found the actual press release (Release ID 2186639, posted 2025-11-05 14:34, MeitY under IndiaAI Mission). It links to the same PDF that was staged.

The release date rested on secondary sources and was marked unconfirmed. The PIB release confirms 2025-11-05. The document body does state the July 2025 committee formation. The Feb 2026 PIB 8-page summary is a separate summary document. I read only its first page. I found no 2026 revision or supersession by web search, and I did not check the MeitY/IndiaAI sites directly.
The summary said India 'does not create a separate AI law'. The text says only that a separate law is not needed at this stage (p.12). Part 3 lists drafting new laws as a long-term step.

The note said the whole document targets all AI developers and deployers and 'has no binding force' as a stated fact. In the text, only the Part 4 industry guidance addresses that group, and the regulator guidance addresses agencies and regulators. The non-binding status is inferred from the recommending wording, not stated by the document.
The first pitfall said India has no AI law, which is not what the text says. The third pitfall said the date was unconfirmed, which is now outdated.

The issuer line said only 'MeitY committee, posted on PIB'. The release and Annexure 1 show MeitY released it under IndiaAI Mission, and the committee was chaired by Balaraman Ravindran (IIT Madras). I added the PIB release ID to the edition.
The note said the release date and later revisions were unverified. The release date is now verified, and the note records that no revision turned up in search.

The note said no reuse statement was found and PIB policy was not re-checked. I fetched the PIB Copyright Policy. It allows free reproduction without prior approval, with conditions: accurate reproduction, a prominent source credit, and third-party material excluded. It covers material on 'this website'. The PDF is on static.pib.gov.in, was written by a committee that includes external members, and carries no licence text of its own (checked in the extract). Whether the policy covers this PDF is therefore not certain. The note now cites exactly this evidence. The decision stays local-only.
The anchor sits in the Executive Summary's Part 1 summary (PDF p.7), not in the Part 1 body (PDF p.15). The ref now says so. The paraphrase matches the summary text.
POL-22 (per-execution authorisation) is only loosely tied to a general safety and robustness principle. It is not clearly wrong, so I left it in.

The passage is about safeguards where direct human oversight is ineffective, such as high-speed trading. It does not address agentic AI. Theme changed from agentic_ai to human_oversight. The text, anchor and POL mappings are correct.
'정기' is the text's 'regular', not a time limit. The text sets no period. I left it as is.
It said the ledger 'proves' the deployer's due diligence. Rephrased to say the approval records can be used as material showing it.

원문은 '콘텐츠 출처(provenance)와 관련된' 생성 콘텐츠의 성능·신뢰 특성에 대한 실시간 모니터링인데 이 한정을 빠뜨려 일반적 콘텐츠 모니터링처럼 읽혔다. gateway_control_ko도 도구 호출 이상 경보를 이 조치의 구현처럼 서술했다.

EO 14110 폐지를 '스카우트 보고, 미확인'으로만 적고 발간일도 없었다. Federal Register(90 FR 8237)에서 EO 14148(2025-01-20 서명) 제2절이 EO 14110을 폐지 대상으로 열거함을 확인했다. NIST 발간물 페이지에서 발간일 2024-07-26을 확인했고, 2026-10-17 기준 AI RMF 페이지에 철회 공지가 없고 'AI RMF 1.0 개정 중' 안내가 있음을 확인해 반영했다.
폐지 사실을 확인하지 않았다는 문구와 '최종판 기준' 서술이 확인 결과와 맞지 않았다. 확인 결과로 갱신하고 AI RMF 개정 중이라는 주의와 MG-3.2-006 범위 주의를 추가했다.
'최종판'은 문서 본문에 없는 표현이다. 발간본으로 바꾸고 64쪽이 PDF 기준임을 명시했다.

defect_list.description: The obligation said the maturity model 'requires' Level 4 (JIT access, two-gate approval, 6-month search plus 12-month retrieval). The memo's schedule (p.4) requires only Level 3 within 320 days, and Level 4 has no deadline. Marked mandatory without that qualification.

The note told readers to cite Appendix B as the minimum without saying the two retention figures disagree. Appendix B item 1 says 'must' 6 months searchable plus 1 year retrievable, but those numbers equal Level 4 in Appendix C. Level 3, the required end state, is only 3 months searchable plus 12 months retrievable.

The controls were written as things the product already does or provides. They also contained unsupported product-status statements: 'currently only OTLP traces and hashed audit export exist, SIEM forwarding is planned'; 'arguments over 300 characters stored as prefix plus hash'; 'provide 6/12 months as federal default'. None of this comes from the document, and the 300-character rule is not found in the gateway source I grepped.

theme was incident_reporting. The provision defines which logs to collect and automated alerts, not notification of an incident to anyone, so logging_records fits better. The gateway control also omitted the automated-alert limb.
POL-48 covers cleanup of temporary files and caches at disconnection. It does not concern audit-log retention.

The memo encourages time sources 'traceable to' the U.S. Naval Observatory or NIST 'where feasible'. The note said 'authoritative sources such as USNO or NIST', dropping 'traceable' and 'where feasible'.
The note said the memo does not apply to private companies. Page 2 puts systems operated by third parties on an agency's behalf in scope. The memo is addressed only to agency heads.
Said the body mentions AI only briefly. The AI mentions are in body p.1 (threat actors), Appendix A (LRA discussion of AI) and Appendix C Level 4 (ML/AI tuning).

The notice put a paraphrase in quotation marks as if verbatim and omitted the sentence that the US Government may hold copyrights transferred by assignment or bequest. The reason also asserted 'no third-party content' without limiting it to what was read. I re-fetched https://www.whitehouse.gov/copyright/ today and it confirms 'government-produced materials ... are not copyright protected'. The PDF itself carries no copyright or licence text. The public-under-license decision is consistent with the central evidence, so the label is unchanged.

The text lists verifying web downloads as a mitigation: 'this includes verifying'. The note said it 'must be verified' (검증해야 한다). The actor was 'deployer', but the text means the downloader of training data, i.e. the model developer. gateway_control_ko presented an analogy to MCP server artifacts as an existing function.
The source says risks 'can be reduced by' understanding models as untrusted components. The note turned this into an instruction ('설계하라고 한다'). It also stated the scanning limitation too absolutely.
The source says identity verification and incentive policies 'may enhance the efficacy'. The note said they raise it (효과를 높인다).

The source calls this one of the 'potential mitigations' that rely on designing systems under the assumption that the model can produce malicious output. The note said the document 'tells you to design' that way (설계하라고 한다).

The note said mitigation 'must combine' (결합해야 한다). The source says it 'requires a multifaceted approach'. pol_ids POL-03 (security update support) and POL-39 (fixing known vulnerabilities) have no basis in the passage or in gateway_control_ko, so they were removed.
gateway_control_ko said that not following extra instructions in server descriptions is something the product does. That is agent-side behaviour (POL-04), not something the gateway guarantees.
POL-33 (data transfer between MCP servers) does not fit exfiltration to an attacker URL or mailbox.
The source addresses organisations in general, not specifically the deployer. Actor changed to 'any'.

The note said chapter 4 covers scale, supply chain and risk management, and that every attack type has a NISTAML identifier. Chapter 4 also covers trade-offs, theoretical limits, evaluation, multimodal and quantized models. The index covers the main attack types, not every type.

The note said input validation makes sure malicious input is 'not passed' to the AI system. The text only says it reduces the risk of such input being passed.

It claimed MINT preserves normal/attack test results as evidence of release testing. The provision concerns external audits of the deployer's AI system. I recast it as an organisational procedure with an evidence attachment as a candidate.

It claimed responses are logged as 'hash/size/result' (unsupported detail). It also did not say that model-internal intermediate-state logs are outside the gateway.
The claim that admin routes require admin authentication is unsupported. Admin MFA and PAW (privileged access workstations) belong to the organisation's IdP and endpoints.
The gateway was credited with OAuth token validation, which POL-21 assigns to HTTP OAuth servers. I rephrased it as a separate POL-21 requirement.
The undefined term '계약 잠금' was removed. I added that signature and checksum verification of model artifacts sits in the deployer's model repository, not the gateway.

The text says a transparent AI system 'informs' stakeholders, and 'can inform and explain' when decisions are automated (bilər). The note wrote 'must be able to explain' (있어야 한다). The condition that metadata was recorded at collection was also turned into a looser conditional.
The text says control points 'should be defined' (təyin olunmalıdır) and that they can be set periodically or at decision points. The note only said they 'can be set'.

The text says a reliable AI system 'gives' consistent results, which is descriptive. The note said it 'must' (내야 한다).
